Adriana, why is your attrition so high?
That is a fair question. Could you tell me which period you are asking about? The last quarter and the last three years look very different.
The last quarter. And I am assuming it is about pay.
That is the assumption everybody starts with, and it is our blind spot. May I ask what you have seen in the other regions?
The same pattern, honestly. So what is your answer?
Let me be candid. The first month is where we lose people, and the two sites with the most overtime are the two sites we lose them from.
And how much has that cost us this year?
I do not have that figure with me, and I am not going to guess in front of this group. I will follow up by Friday with the cost per exit.

Before I answer that, may I give you some context?
Let me clarify. What I mean is that the first month is the problem.

If there is one takeaway, it is the two sites.

I coach executives for a living, and the thing people ask me about most is the question they did not prepare. Here is what I tell them. The silence after a hard question is never as long as it feels. Three seconds sounds like thirty inside your head and like nothing in the room. So use them. The second thing is that you are allowed to ask before you answer. Could you tell me which period you are asking about? That single sentence buys you time and makes the answer better, because half the hard questions in a meeting are hard only because they are vague. And the third thing: when you genuinely do not know, say it and give a date. I do not have that number with me, and I will send it to you by Friday. Nobody has ever lost credibility for that sentence.

Adriana, quick one before Thursday. I want you to know how that room works, because it is not the same as ours. The vice president asks one question and then says nothing for a long time. Do not fill the silence: he is waiting to see whether you add something you were not asked. The finance director interrupts, always, and never to attack you; he is checking whether you know the number well enough to keep going. And the head of operations asks the same question twice with different words. If you notice that, it is not a trap, it is how he thinks. One last thing: none of them will ask you anything about your English. That is a conversation only you are having.
